correctness.rationale: Writing k for the number of opposite-spin pairs gives H/J=2s²−n+(K/J−1)(n−2k)−2(h/J)s, because the all-edge interaction depends only on total magnetization 2s. The constraints on pair counts give exactly k=0 or 1 through n−|s| in steps of two, according to the parity of n−|s|. The sign of K−J thus selects the minimum or maximum feasible k, and all k tie at equality. Choosing the pair types and opposite-pair orientations gives every stated multiplicity. Forward sector differences divided by 2J are t_s−t; for 0<K<J the consecutive threshold gaps alternate between 2K/J and 4−2K/J, both positive, and for K≥J the gap is 2. At K=0 the gap of the first type vanishes, giving exactly the listed triple transitions, including s=−1,0,1 at zero field for odd n. Spin reversal supplies all other signed cases. At fixed unscaled couplings and field, |s| is bounded uniformly in n, so the sector counts have exponential rates n log 2 off K=J and 2n log 2 on it; summing the at most three coexisting sectors preserves the rate.
residual_risks: The finite verifier compares the all-edge magnetization identity plus the pair sum against the sector formula, not a separately written edge-by-edge Hamiltonian. Its reported tests are supplementary; the derivation above does not rely on them. Entropy is for exactly zero temperature and fixed parameters, not a scaling limit with n-dependent K−J.

evidence: The complete-graph case follows from fixed total magnetization and binomial counting. For general K, a sufficiently strong exact joint partition function would preempt the finite sector claim: its coefficients would count the p,q,k pair types at each energy and magnetization. None of the inspected partition functions has these interactions.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Knowing the K=J count loses all information about which k values minimize and with what parity when K≠J. A general method for exact finite partition sums does not by itself provide the perturbed sector counts and their asymptotics. The finding is not credited with inventing the multinomial counting technique.

evidence: The natural equivalent model is an all-pairs Ising antiferromagnet with a correction (K−J) on the perfect matching. The cited long-range antiferromagnets are quantum transverse-field/two-sublattice models; the cited dimer paper starts from a random short-range spin glass.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Grouping the present spins as dimers leaves a deterministic quadratic term in total magnetization and an independent intra-pair correction. Neither the quantum two-sublattice separation nor a short-range dimer approximation gives this Hamiltonian or exact degeneracies.

originality.rationale: The supported distinct claim is the exact ground-sector classification of the deterministic matching deformation for all couplings and fields in scope, with the triple crossings and residual entropy contrast. The unperturbed complete-graph case is routine and not credited separately. Related exact solutions use different graphs, interaction signs, or spin spaces and do not give this matching deformation.
residual_risks: An equivalent classical all-to-all paired model or a complete joint energy–magnetization partition sum under block-spin terminology may remain unindexed. The three-state Potts catalogue hit was compared only at summary level.

value.rationale: The perturbation continuously connects two standard highly symmetric graph models, rather than selecting an arbitrary field grid. It separates which types of configurations carry the residual entropy: essentially aligned pairs below equal coupling, opposite pairs above it, and both kinds available without a matching-energy penalty on the equality line. The exact field transitions, triple degeneracies at the deleted matching, and quantitative entropy contrast give a usable zero-temperature benchmark across the deformation.
residual_risks: This is a structurally simple solvable family; value is in the full classification and entropy comparison, not a new general phase-transition technique or a finite-temperature claim.
